title: Africa Digital ID Radar, 24 Nov 2026: 39 instant payment systems, NIN via WhatsApp, Rwanda ID registration
sum: AfricaNenda's fifth SIIPS report counts 39 live instant payment systems; Nigeria's NIMC plans WhatsApp pre-enrollment for NIN; Rwanda reopens Single Digital ID registration; Kenya joins the Digital Public Goods Alliance.
body: This edition covers four developments from 17–19 November 2026: a new continental ranking of inclusive instant payment systems, Nigeria's plan to start national ID enrollment through WhatsApp, the reopening of Rwanda's Single Digital ID registration, and new members of the Digital Public Goods Alliance, including Kenya.

Key developments
  • Africa · Instant payments (19 Nov): The AfricaNenda Foundation's fifth State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems in Africa (SIIPS) report, produced with UNECA and the World Bank Group, assessed 39 live systems, up from 29 in the 2022 edition. The basic inclusivity tier grew from 15 to 19 systems: Kenya's PesaLink, Sierra Leone's Salone Payment Switch and SADC's TCIB moved up after adding person-to-business payments, and Liberia's Pay Na-Na, BurundiPay and Guinea's Mojaloop-based NimbaPay entered for the first time. WAEMU's PI-SPI entered at the progressed tier, and Nigeria's NIBSS Instant Payment remains the only system rated mature. Liberia's central bank plans a national electronic payment switch built on Pay Na-Na for the first quarter of 2027. Sources: MyJoyOnline; Vanguard
  • Nigeria · National ID (18 Nov): NIMC Director-General Abisoye Coker-Odusote said the commission plans to let Nigerians start NIN registration on WhatsApp, with pre-enrollment and booking of biometric capture appointments; no launch date was given. NIMC is also working with JAMB so exam candidates can verify their identity with their NIN before registering. Source: BusinessDay
  • Rwanda · Single Digital ID (17 Nov): Registration for the Single Digital ID resumed in all districts on 17 November for people who missed the first exercise, and runs until 16 January 2027. Source: The New Times
  • Kenya · Digital public goods (18 Nov): At its annual members meeting in Paris, the Digital Public Goods Alliance welcomed four new members, Kenya, Kazakhstan, the Center for Digital Public Infrastructure (CDPI) and the Inria Foundation, taking membership to 60. CDPI, which has advised more than 25 countries, plans vendor-neutral technical advice and short bootcamps for government engineering teams. Source: Biometric Update
Why it matters

Instant payment rails are spreading quickly across Africa, and each step toward person-to-business and government payments raises the need for strong customer identification and fraud controls; see Fraud Prevention. At the same time, Nigeria and Rwanda are widening enrollment channels for foundational ID, and Kenya's DPGA membership adds weight to open, interoperable stacks such as MOSIP; see MOSIP Integration and Identity Management System.
Sources: MyJoyOnline (19 Nov 2026); Vanguard (Nov 2026); BusinessDay (18 Nov 2026); The New Times (17 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (18 Nov 2026)

title: Italy opens new IT-Wallet phase: digital driving license now valid as an identity document
sum: Italy's IT-Wallet in the IO app entered a new trial phase on 23 November 2026 with up to 100,000 users, recognizing the digital driving license as ID and adding diplomas, residence certificates and a wallet login.
body: Italy began a new trial phase of its public IT-Wallet on 23 November 2026. The wallet sits inside the IO app, developed by PagoPA with Sogei as technology partner and coordinated by the Department for Digital Transformation. The first group is limited to 100,000 people, chosen at random from IO users who hold an electronic identity card (CIE) and taking part voluntarily. The rollout has three stages, and the wallet is expected to open to everyone once the trial ends.

The main change is that the digital driving license can now be shown as an identity document, not only as proof of the right to drive; the digital health card and the European Disability Card get the same status. New credentials include residence certificates, school diplomas, attendance certificates, university degrees and enrollment records, and wallet documents can replace physical versions wherever the originals are accepted. The wallet also includes IT-Wallet ID, issued by the Istituto Poligrafico e Zecca dello Stato, and becomes a login method, with an "Entra con IT-Wallet" button appearing gradually on public administration sites. A free app, Valida Documenti, lets staff check documents.

Activation requires a CIE and an NFC-enabled phone, including for users who sign in to IO with SPID. The earlier Documenti su IO service, which has had 13 million activations, keeps working with limited functions until July 2027. Undersecretary for technological innovation Alessio Butti said IT-Wallet adds security, documents and functions in line with European objectives.

Key facts
  • New IT-Wallet phase started 23 November 2026, first group of up to 100,000 CIE holders
  • Digital driving license, health card and European Disability Card accepted as identity documents
  • New credentials: residence certificates, diplomas, degrees, enrollment records
  • "Entra con IT-Wallet" login and Valida Documenti verification app
  • Activation needs CIE plus NFC phone; Documenti su IO usable until July 2027
Why it matters

Italy is one of the first EU member states to make wallet credentials legally equivalent to physical ID and to use the wallet as a login, ahead of the EUDI Wallet deadline at the end of 2026. Relying parties will need verifier tools and NFC-based onboarding that work with a national eID chip; see Digital ID Wallet, National eID Trust and eIDAS Readiness.
Sources: ID Tech (23 Nov 2026)

title: UK ICO audit of Met Police facial recognition makes 29 recommendations, three urgent
sum: The UK Information Commissioner's Office gave the Metropolitan Police 'reasonable' assurance on live and retrospective facial recognition but flagged three urgent gaps in retrospective searches.
body: The UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) has published the executive summary of its data protection audit of the Metropolitan Police Service's use of facial recognition. It makes 29 recommendations: 11 for live facial recognition (LFR) and 18 for retrospective facial recognition (RFR). Three RFR recommendations are rated urgent and 11 more are high priority. Overall, the ICO gave both technologies a "reasonable" assurance rating. Operator-initiated facial recognition, which the Met is trialling on officers' phones, was not covered.

On LFR, the ICO found that training is not refreshed, completion rates are not formally recorded and staff understanding of breach reporting is uneven. On RFR, it said the Data Protection Officer appeared detached from oversight; staff search the Police National Database only when the Met's internal Reveal system returns no match, a process that is poorly documented; and the ICO could not confirm that investigators follow retention rules for probe images. It also noted that policies, impact assessments and regular technology assessments are in place.

Key facts
  • 29 recommendations: 11 for LFR, 18 for RFR
  • 3 urgent and 11 high-priority recommendations, all for RFR
  • Overall rating: "reasonable" assurance for both technologies
  • Gaps: DPO oversight, documentation of Police National Database searches, retention of probe images
  • Operator-initiated facial recognition not in scope
Why it matters

Regulators are moving from debating live facial recognition to auditing how retrospective searches against existing image databases are governed. Any agency or vendor running 1:N face matching will be expected to show clear audit trails, retention controls and human review; see Face Biometrics, SAVIS ABIS and Consent Management.
Sources: Biometric Update (23 Nov 2026)

title: Africa Digital ID Radar, 22 Nov 2026: Egypt aligns with eIDAS, Liberia rejects ID deal, SIM-based checks
sum: Egypt becomes the first non-European country technically aligned with EU e-signature rules; Liberia's lawmakers reject a US$52m ID concession; MTN's Bayobab and Google Firebase replace SMS OTPs; South Africa adds passports at 480 bank branches.
body: The first Africa Digital ID Radar covers five developments from 16–20 November 2026: cross-border recognition of Egyptian e-signatures in the EU, a parliamentary rejection of a national ID concession in Liberia, operator-based phone number checks across MTN markets, wider passport access through South African banks, and a growing cybersecurity skills gap around African ID systems.

Key developments
  • Egypt · Trust services (16 Nov): After assessing Egypt's Trusted List for electronic signatures and seals under eIDAS, the European Commission found the framework technically aligned with EU rules, making Egypt the first country outside Europe to reach this status. Egypt will be added to the EU Third Countries Trusted List. ITIDA chief executive Ahmed Elzaher and DG CONNECT director-general Roberto Viola signed an Administrative Arrangement under which each side references the other's trusted lists. Source: ID Tech Wire
  • Liberia · National ID (18 Nov): Lawmakers sent a proposed US$52 million, 10-year build-operate-transfer contract with OeSD International back to President Joseph Boakai for renegotiation. A House joint committee listed more than 40 alleged deficiencies, said the deal broke procurement rules because open international competitive bidding was not used, and warned about biometric data sovereignty and the National Identification Registry's authority. Source: Biometric Update
  • Pan-African · Phone verification (20 Nov): Bayobab, part of MTN Digital Infrastructure, and Google Firebase launched carrier-based phone number verification for Android apps. The check runs silently through Bayobab's network APIs instead of SMS one-time passcodes, with SMS as a fallback. MTN serves about 165 million Android subscribers. Source: ID Tech Wire
  • South Africa · Passports and smart ID (18 Nov): Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber said adults can now apply for passports at 480 bank branches (412 Capitec, 68 Absa), taking the service to more than 700 locations. Green ID book holders apply for a smart ID at the same time. Over 1 million smart ID applications have gone through banks in eight months. Source: ID Tech Wire
  • Africa · Cybersecurity (19 Nov): A Biometric Update feature cites estimates of a gap of at least 200,000 cybersecurity professionals in Africa and World Bank data showing only 17 African countries had CSIRTs registered with FIRST as of January 2025, and recalls a cyberattack that halted Senegal's ID issuance for several days. Source: Biometric Update
Why it matters

Egypt's alignment shows that African trust service providers can gain EU recognition through trusted-list interoperability, a model other countries can follow with an eIDAS readiness program. Liberia's case shows how closely parliaments now examine data sovereignty and procurement in ID deals, while SIM-based checks and bank-branch enrollment widen the base for identity verification. The skills gap makes a security operations center part of the core infrastructure for national ID.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (16 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (18 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (20 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (18 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (19 Nov 2026)

title: Dutch data protection authority finds AI camera glasses fail privacy and security tests
sum: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens tested six AI camera glasses sold in the Netherlands and found weak recording indicators, security flaws and unreliable AI advice, and advised consumers not to buy them for general use.
body: The Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, AP) has tested six pairs of AI camera glasses on sale in the Netherlands, priced from under €100 to over €500, and concluded that their privacy safeguards do not work in practice. Two devices were tested further in simulated personal-safety situations. The AP did not name the manufacturers and described the work as a sample rather than a ranking.

On almost every device the recording light was hard to see or easy to cover, and most glasses kept recording when the light was covered. Several devices had weaknesses that could let a nearby person connect without permission, reach recordings or operate the camera. Users were not always told where their data was processed, and AI processing often took place on servers outside the EU. In one simulated resuscitation, a device repeatedly said an ambulance was coming although no call had been made. The AP advised consumers against buying the glasses for everyday use.

Separately, consumer group Consumentenbond is suing Meta over its camera glasses, arguing they capture bystanders without consent in breach of Dutch and EU privacy law; a hearing is scheduled for 26 November 2026 in Amsterdam.

Key facts
  • Six AI camera glasses tested; prices from under €100 to over €500
  • Recording indicators hard to see or easy to cover; most devices kept recording when covered
  • Security flaws could allow unauthorised connection, access to recordings or camera control
  • AI data often processed on servers outside the EU
  • AP advises consumers not to buy the devices for general use
  • Consumentenbond v Meta hearing: 26 November 2026, Amsterdam
Why it matters

Wearable cameras bring face capture into everyday public spaces, so regulators are judging them on whether bystanders can see and control recording. Device makers and integrators will need visible, tamper-resistant indicators, secure pairing and clear consent management, and any AI camera or face biometrics feature will be held to GDPR standards on where and how data is processed.
Sources: Biometric Update (21 Nov 2026)

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 21 Nov 2026: no digital euro deal, Italy wallet age checks, Met Police phone FR
sum: Digital euro negotiators miss a deal and plan December talks; Italy's governing parties propose age checks compatible with EUDI wallets; London police trial phone-based facial recognition; youniqx opens a public EUDI sandbox.
body: This edition covers five developments from 18–20 November 2026: the outcome of the latest digital euro negotiations, an Italian proposal tying social media age checks to EU wallets, a facial recognition pilot by London's Metropolitan Police, a public test environment for EUDI wallets, and EU funding for deepfake detection.

Key developments
  • EU · Digital euro (19 Nov): Parliament and Irish Council Presidency negotiators failed to reach a political agreement during the night of 18–19 November; a parliamentary source said the agenda was too heavy. A staggered roll-out appears agreed, while holding-limit procedure, exceptions to mandatory shop acceptance and the PSP remuneration model remain open. New sessions are suggested for 3 and 16 December, and the Council wants to conclude before year-end. Source: Agence Europe
  • Italy · Age verification (20 Nov): Governing parties filed an amendment, now before the Chamber of Deputies' Justice Committee, setting 15 as the minimum age to open a social media account alone, with parent-linked accounts from 13. Platforms would verify age with a solution interoperable with European digital identity wallets; AGCOM would have nine months to set technical rules. The amendment is not yet adopted. Source: ID Tech Wire
  • UK · Facial recognition (20 Nov): The Metropolitan Police began a six-month trial of Operator Initiated Facial Recognition, letting 100 trained officers photograph a person on a force phone and compare it with custody images; every possible match is reviewed by an officer. It will not be used on anyone believed to be under 13. Liberty called for a pause until legislation is in place. Source: ID Tech Wire
  • Austria · EUDI Wallet (18–19 Nov): youniqx Identity, part of the Austrian State Printing Group, opened a public EUDI sandbox where developers can test fictional PID credentials in scenarios such as hotel booking, alcohol purchase and SIM registration, and relaunched its MIA app as an EUDI wallet on iOS, with Android to follow. Sources: Biometric Update; GlobeNewswire
  • Italy · Deepfake detection (20 Nov): identifAI is one of 35 companies selected from 453 full applications for a €2.5 million EIC Accelerator grant, with possible equity of up to €10 million; the EIC proposes €84 million in total grants, with agreements expected within three months. Source: Biometric Update
Why it matters

Age assurance is becoming one of the first mass-market uses for EUDI wallets, as Italy follows Poland in naming wallet-based checks. Public sandboxes help relying parties prepare before national wallets go live, while police and platform use of face matching keeps attention on liveness, deepfake defense and oversight; see Digital ID Wallet, Liveness & Deepfake Defense and Face Biometrics.
Sources: Agence Europe (19 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (20 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (20 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (19 Nov 2026); GlobeNewswire (18 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (20 Nov 2026).

title: Germany's Bundesrat approves Digital Identities Act, clearing d-you EUDI Wallet for 2 January 2027 launch
sum: Germany's federal states unanimously backed the Digital Identities Act, the last parliamentary step before the d-you EU Digital Identity Wallet launches on 2 January 2027 with ID, age checks, bank onboarding and contract signing.
body: Germany's Bundesrat, the chamber representing the federal states, unanimously approved the Digital Identities Act on Friday 20 November 2026, ID Tech Wire reported. The Bundestag had passed the law in mid-October with the votes of the CDU/CSU and SPD. With the states' consent, the act can now be signed and promulgated, and it takes effect the day after promulgation.

The law provides the legal basis for d-you, Germany's EU Digital Identity Wallet, which is due to be available from 2 January 2027. Use is free and voluntary, and non-digital services remain available. From launch, users should be able to identify themselves, prove their age, open bank accounts and sign legally binding contracts. About 40 partners from industry, academia and government are involved; more than 300 use cases have been prepared and about 50 are expected at launch, with items such as birth certificates and tickets to follow.

Setting up the wallet requires a German ID card or electronic residence permit with the online ID function activated and its six-digit PIN; the card data is read over NFC. According to the developers, phones need at least iOS 26.4 or Android 14, NFC and the necessary security features. An internet connection is required at first, with fully offline use planned later. A digital driving license is scheduled to be available in d-you from 2 January; at a roadside check, the driver scans a QR code shown by police and approves which data is shared. The license supplements the plastic card rather than replacing it.

Key facts
  • Bundesrat approval: unanimous, 20 November 2026; Bundestag passed the act in mid-October 2026.
  • Entry into force: the day after promulgation.
  • d-you launch: 2 January 2027; free and voluntary.
  • About 50 of more than 300 prepared use cases expected at launch, including ID, age checks, bank account opening and contract signing.
  • Requirements: eID-enabled German ID card or residence permit, PIN, NFC phone with iOS 26.4 or Android 14 or later.
  • The act also lets people who apply for an ID card at 70 or older keep it indefinitely.
Why it matters

With the law in place, Germany is set to meet the EU's end-2026 wallet deadline using its existing eID card as the anchor. Banks, retailers and online platforms that want to accept d-you will need relying-party integration for presentation flows, age-over checks and qualified signatures; see Digital ID Wallet, eIDAS 2.0 Readiness and Remote Signing.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (20 Nov 2026).

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 20 Nov 2026: Poland's wallet age checks, Milan eGates award, MiDNI court order
sum: Poland plans age checks via mObywatel or the EUDI Wallet for an under-15 social media ban; Milan airports award Vision-Box €6.9m for eGates; Spain's Supreme Court orders checks on 61,603 MiDNI readers.

sources.name: ID Tech Wire – Poland age checks

body: This edition covers four developments from 18–19 November 2026: Poland's plan to use its national app or the EU wallet for social media age checks, a biometric border contract at Milan's airports, a court order on Spain's digital ID readers before the general election, and the UK biometrics commissioner's response to the government's facial recognition plans.

Key facts
  • Poland: Deputy Digital Affairs Minister Dariusz Standerski told a Sejm committee that a planned law setting 15 as the minimum age for social media accounts would let users prove age through mObywatel, the EU Digital Identity Wallet, or a platform tool that meets EU rules. Only an over/under-15 answer would be shared, and biometrics are not planned. Accounts created before 1 September 2017 and accounts with confirmed identity are exempt. The draft is not yet adopted. ID Tech Wire, 19 Nov
  • Italy: SEA, operator of Linate and Malpensa airports, awarded Vision-Box €6,867,768 for new automated border control eGates, upgrades to existing gates, and a trial of pre-border kiosks and a biometric corridor at Malpensa. The award notice (798765-2026) was published in TED on 17 November 2026; Vision-Box was the only bidder. ID Tech Wire, 19 Nov
  • Spain: The Supreme Court ordered the Interior Ministry to certify within two days whether security checks were done on the 61,603 devices that polling stations will use to verify voters showing the MiDNI digital ID at the 29 November general election. The readers were rented under an emergency, directly awarded contract worth €7,000,455 including VAT. ID Tech Wire, 18 Nov
  • UK: Biometrics and Surveillance Camera Commissioner William Webster called the government's response to its facial recognition consultation an important step toward legislation, but asked for more detail on necessity, proportionality and oversight powers, and for statutory codes of practice for police and commercial users. Biometric Update, 18 Nov
Why it matters

Age assurance is becoming one of the first mass use cases for national wallets, while border and election deployments show that biometric and digital ID readers now need documented security checks and clear oversight. Both trends favor privacy-preserving wallet-based attestations, certified face biometrics and auditable national eID trust services.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (19 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (19 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (18 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (18 Nov 2026)

title: EU publishes first Cyber Resilience Act standards: EN 40000-1-1 and EN 40000-1-2
sum: CEN and CENELEC published the first two European standards supporting the Cyber Resilience Act, covering common vocabulary and lifecycle cybersecurity risk management for products with digital elements; more than 30 further standards are in preparation.

sources.name: European Commission – Shaping Europe's digital future

body: The first European standards supporting the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) were published on 18 November 2026, the European Commission announced on 19 November. CEN and CENELEC released two parts of the new EN 40000 series: EN 40000-1-1, which sets the vocabulary for the series, and EN 40000-1-2, which sets principles, product risk management and lifecycle activities for products with digital elements.

EN 40000-1-2 gives manufacturers a common way to identify, assess and manage cybersecurity risk from design and production through maintenance, end of support and decommissioning. According to the Commission it applies to a wide range of products, from connected door locks and routers to microcontrollers, operating systems, browsers and password managers. Product-category standards will build on it.

The standards were developed in CEN-CLC/JTC 13/WG 9 under standardization request M/606, which the Commission sent to CEN, CENELEC and ETSI in February 2025. The Commission says more than 30 further standards are in preparation; CEN-CENELEC names FprEN 40000-1-3 and the first product-specific standards as next.

Key facts
  • Published 18 November 2026; announced by the Commission on 19 November
  • EN 40000-1-1: vocabulary for the EN 40000 series
  • EN 40000-1-2: principles, product risk management and lifecycle activities
  • Requested under standardization request M/606 (February 2025)
  • More than 30 further CRA standards in preparation
  • Available through national standards bodies on their own publication schedules
Why it matters

The EN 40000 base standards give manufacturers of connected products a shared reference for building security into the whole lifecycle before CRA obligations apply. Vendors of devices, firmware and software can start mapping their processes now, covering IoT device security, secure update and key handling with crypto-agility, and wider cybersecurity practices.
Sources: European Commission (19 Nov 2026); CEN-CENELEC (19 Nov 2026)

title: Tanzania launches new national ID card with eight data sections and NIDA Wallet app
sum: Tanzania's NIDA launched a redesigned biometric ID card with room for eight linked services and a NIDA Wallet mobile app, backed by five production machines printing about 2,800 cards an hour.
body: Tanzania has launched a new edition of its national ID card and a NIDA Wallet mobile app. Prime Minister Mwigulu Nchemba presided over the ceremony in Kibaha, Pwani region, on 18 November 2026 on behalf of President Samia Suluhu Hassan, and also launched a new card-production system and 10 vehicles for registration officers. Emptech is NIDA's technology and implementation partner.

The card doubles the number of information sections from four to eight. According to NIDA Director General James Kaji, these will gradually hold birth certificate details, health insurance records, taxpayer identification numbers, blood group, driving license and marital status, depending on each institution's readiness and legal basis. Personal data is now laser engraved rather than surface printed, with color-changing elements, tactile marks, a machine-readable zone and a QR code.

More than TZS 30 billion (about US$11.4 million) went into the new cards and five production machines, which together print around 2,800 cards an hour. NIDA expects the extra capacity to clear the card backlog within two months, and Kaji said ID numbers alone will stop being accepted for services in three months. As of 29 October, 27,648,911 Tanzanians were registered, and more than 72 government and 85 private institutions are connected to NIDA. The NIDA Wallet extends the ID to phones for presenting credentials, managing authorisations and sharing information with participating services.

Key facts
  • Launched 18 November 2026 in Kibaha, Pwani region
  • Eight information sections, up from four; existing cards remain valid
  • Five machines, about 2,800 cards per hour; investment over TZS 30 billion
  • 27,648,911 people registered as of 29 October 2026
  • ID numbers without a physical card to stop being accepted in three months
  • NIDA Wallet app brings the national ID to mobile phones
Why it matters

Tanzania is pairing a multi-application card with a mobile wallet, so the national ID becomes a hub that sector registries link into. This depends on a robust identity management system, high-volume personalization and secure digital ID wallet issuance, alongside interoperable registration through an enrollment suite as NIDA extends numbers to newborns.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (19 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (20 Nov 2026)

title: Bulgaria's cabinet approves EU Digital Identity Wallet bill and opens the BG Wallet information site
sum: Bulgaria's Council of Ministers approved a draft law setting the legal framework for BG Wallet, the national EUDI Wallet, and the digital ministry launched wallet.gov.bg; parliament is asked to pass it by the end of 2026.
body: Bulgaria's Council of Ministers approved a draft Law on the European Digital Identity Wallet on 19 November 2026. The bill sets the national legal and institutional framework for BG Wallet, Bulgaria's version of the EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet, and now goes to the National Assembly. At the same time, the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation launched wallet.gov.bg, an information site that explains how phone-based identity verification will work, which documents can be used, and answers common questions.

Under the draft, using the wallet is voluntary and free of charge. Citizens will be able to request, store and present identity data and electronic attestations for public, private and cross-border services, and to create qualified electronic signatures. The bill also sets rules on wallet certification, supervision of wallet providers, vulnerability response, security and data protection. The ministry was designated as the supervisory authority for wallet providers by a cabinet decision in September 2026.

Minister Ivan Vasilev said the government wants the National Assembly to adopt the law by the end of 2026, so that Bulgaria meets its commitment to the European Commission; EU rules require member states to provide EUDI Wallets by the end of 2026. BG Wallet will roll out in stages, and the mobile app and download links will be published on wallet.gov.bg later.

Key facts
  • Cabinet approval of the draft EUDI Wallet law: 19 November 2026; next step is the National Assembly.
  • Wallet use is voluntary and free; qualified electronic signatures are supported.
  • The bill covers wallet certification, provider supervision, vulnerability handling, security and data protection.
  • Supervisory authority: Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation (designated September 2026).
  • Target: parliamentary adoption by the end of 2026; app release date to be announced on wallet.gov.bg.
Why it matters

Bulgaria joins Poland in moving the legal basis for its national wallet only weeks before the EU deadline, which means certification, provider supervision and relying-party onboarding will have to run in parallel. Governments and banks preparing for this phase need digital ID wallet infrastructure, eIDAS 2.0 readiness work and remote qualified signing that can plug into the wallet from day one.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (19 Nov 2026)

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 19 Nov 2026: Poland's wallet bill, uncertified wallets, Companies House checks
sum: Poland moves to put the EUDI Wallet in mObywatel; experts say no national wallet is yet listed as certified weeks before the deadline; UK Companies House reaches about 90% identity verification compliance.
body: Wallet readiness dominates this cycle in Europe: Poland has taken the first legislative step toward its EUDI Wallet, industry experts warn of an uneven launch across the EU, and the UK shows what mandatory identity verification looks like after a year in force. No published outcome of the 18 November digital euro trilogue was found at the time of writing.
Key developments
<ul>

• Poland · EUDI Wallet (17 Nov 2026): The Council of Ministers adopted draft amendments to the trust services and electronic identification act so the EU wallet can be offered first inside mObywatel and later as an app update. Planned uses include bank account opening, SIM activation, qualified e-signatures, prescriptions and age checks. Source: ID Tech Wire

• EU · Wallet rollout (18 Nov 2026): In a Biometric Update webinar, experts from Digidentity, the FIDO Alliance and Signicat noted that no national wallet is yet listed as certified on the Commission's eIDAS Dashboard. Signicat's Jon Ølnes said a version with PID, mobile driving license and age verification could be ready now, while full certification may take until late 2027; Digidentity's Fred Slikker said regulators are unlikely to fine anyone on day one. Companies not registered in a member state cannot become relying parties. Source: Biometric Update

• UK · Identity verification (18 Nov 2026): One year after mandatory checks began on 18 Nov 2025, about 90% of active companies comply; more than 12 million director and PSC appointments are verified, and over 75,000 personal data corrections and 14,000 PSC address fixes have been made. All companies must comply or enter enforcement by the end of March 2027; Companies House values full verification at £210–400 million a year. Source: Biometric Update

Key facts
  • Poland: wallet bill adopted by government on 17 Nov 2026; launch date not yet set.
  • EU: no national wallet listed as certified on the eIDAS Dashboard as of 18 Nov 2026.
  • UK: ~90% of active companies compliant; enforcement deadline end of March 2027.
Why it matters

The first wave of EUDI Wallets is likely to arrive with limited functions and staggered certification, so relying parties will keep running existing identity verification alongside wallet acceptance for some time. The UK figures show that mandatory, large-scale verification is workable when backed by enforcement, and that wallet-based digital ID and qualified signing will compete with established onboarding channels.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (17 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (18 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (18 Nov 2026)

title: New Zealand: Verifone brings Kiwi Access digital age checks to 80,000 payment terminals
sum: Verifone has added support for the Kiwi Access proof-of-age credential from the govt.nz app to more than 80,000 Android payment terminals in New Zealand, without new hardware.
body: Verifone has launched support for Kiwi Access, a digital proof-of-age credential, on its payment terminals in New Zealand. The feature runs on more than 80,000 Verifone Android terminals across the country, including the Victa range, without new hardware. The company demonstrated it with NEC New Zealand and Hospitality New Zealand to an audience from government, retail and finance.

A customer presents the credential from the govt.nz app by tap or QR code and approves a consent request on the phone. According to Verifone's Kristy Gregory, the terminal receives only a yes/no answer on whether the credential is registered and the holder is over 18, and no other personal information passes to Verifone. Kiwi Access, which has issued physical over-18 cards for years, is described as progressing through accreditation under the Digital Identity Services Trust Framework. Verifone processes about 700 million transactions a year at more than 90,000 business locations in New Zealand and expects palm and face payments to start there next year.

Key facts
  • More than 80,000 Verifone Android terminals in NZ support Kiwi Access, no new hardware
  • Credential held in the govt.nz app; tap or QR with on-phone consent
  • Terminal receives only "registered" and "over 18" results
  • Kiwi Access progressing through DISTF accreditation
  • Target sectors include liquor, supermarkets, hospitality, pharmacies, telecoms and gambling
Why it matters

Following Cuscal Paymark's plan for its terminals, Verifone's launch means New Zealand's largest point-of-sale networks are becoming verifiers for government wallet credentials, using selective disclosure rather than full ID scans. This creates demand for verifier SDKs, age assurance and biometric payment at the counter; see Decentralized Identity, Digital ID Wallet and Palm Biometric Payment.
Sources: ID Tech (18 Nov 2026)

title: Australia: hijacked Optimizely testing tool planted card skimmers on Vodafone, HSBC and other brands' sites
sum: Attackers abused a flaw in Optimizely Web Experimentation to inject card-skimming and crypto-stealing code into scripts used by at least 178 organizations, including several Australian and New Zealand brands.
body: Attackers exploited a flaw in the signup flow of Optimizely Web Experimentation, a website testing tool, and injected card-skimming and cryptocurrency-stealing JavaScript into scripts served to at least 178 organizations' websites, iTnews reported on 18 November 2026. Named victims include Vodafone Australia, HSBC Australia, Rest Super, TPG Telecom, Betashares, Compare Club and Levi's Australia and New Zealand, as well as global brands such as Zoom, the BBC and CNN.

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the malicious code in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts he checked and traced about US$7,040 to the attacker's wallets. The first injection was at 3:21pm AEDT on Monday 16 November, and most scripts were cleaned by about 8:10am the next day. Unpatched iPhones and iPads were also redirected to exploit kits.

Optimizely said an unauthorised party abused its signup flow; it has blocked the path, deployed a fix, removed the injected code, notified customers and engaged Mandiant. Its interim report says the attacker created accounts from 11:37am AEDT on 16 November by guessing staff email addresses, and delivery was blocked at Cloudflare at 3:06am AEDT on 17 November. TPG said it found no evidence of compromise in Vodafone systems and paused its use of Optimizely; HSBC has reportedly disabled the tool globally. The investigation is ongoing.

Key facts
  • At least 178 organizations affected through a third-party website testing script.
  • Malicious code found in 188 of 1,611 scripts checked by Report URI.
  • Exposure window: about 16 hours, from 16 to 17 November 2026 (AEDT).
  • About US$7,040 traced to attacker wallets so far.
  • Optimizely has fixed the flaw and engaged Mandiant; investigation continues.
Why it matters

The attack shows how a single third-party script can turn trusted bank, telco and super fund pages into card-skimming points, bypassing the organizations' own controls. Strong payment flows rely on transaction signing that does not trust the browser page, continuous security monitoring of client-side code and layered fraud prevention.
Sources: iTnews (18 Nov 2026)

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 18 Nov 2026: CRA guidance in the Official Journal, BundID 2FA, ScotAccount passkeys
sum: Commission CRA guidance is published in the Official Journal; Germany adds email codes to BundID after an automated attack; ScotAccount passes one million accounts; Swiss e-ID opponents launch a new initiative.
body: Cybersecurity and authentication lead this cycle in Europe: new EU guidance on the Cyber Resilience Act, stronger login protection for Germany's citizen account, passkeys for Scotland's digital ID, and renewed political debate over Switzerland's e-ID. The digital euro trilogue scheduled for 18 November had not produced a published outcome at the time of writing.
Key developments
<ul>

• EU · Cyber Resilience Act (17 Nov 2026): The Commission's guidance on applying Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 appeared in the Official Journal as Communication C/2026/6013. Issued under Article 26(1) with a focus on microenterprises and SMEs, it covers scope, open-source software, substantial modifications, support periods, risk assessment and reporting, and is not binding. Reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities has applied since 11 September 2026; the main obligations apply from 11 December 2027. Source: EUR-Lex; Captain Compliance

• Germany · National eID / Cybersecurity (17 Nov 2026): After an unsuccessful automated login attack confirmed by the BSI, BundID now sends an emailed security code for every username-and-password login; affected accounts were blocked and asked to reset passwords. eID card and Elster certificate sign-ins were unaffected. Source: ID Tech Wire

• UK (Scotland) · Digital ID (17 Nov 2026): ScotAccount, launched in 2023, has passed one million registered accounts. Its next phase adds phishing-resistant passkey sign-in, enhanced document verification and more account controls. Verification uses photo ID with face matching, and since August 2026 a HM Passport Office route (passport details plus a selfie). Source: Biometric Update

• Switzerland · e-ID (17 Nov 2026): The Nova committee launched a popular initiative in Bern to guarantee that people without an e-ID are not disadvantaged and to limit use of e-ID data to proofs of identity. It has until 17 May 2028 to collect 100,000 signatures; voters approved the e-ID law in September 2025 with 50.4%. Source: ID Tech Wire

Key facts
  • CRA guidance: C/2026/6013, published 17 Nov 2026; main obligations from 11 Dec 2027.
  • BundID: email one-time code now mandatory for password logins.
  • ScotAccount: more than 1 million accounts; passkeys next.
  • Swiss initiative: 100,000 signatures needed by 17 May 2028.
Why it matters

Regulators and operators are converging on the same message: secure-by-design products and phishing-resistant login are becoming baseline expectations for digital identity services. Vendors supplying wallets and citizen portals will need to show CRA-ready vulnerability handling alongside strong passwordless authentication and reliable identity verification, while the Swiss debate is a reminder that user choice and data minimisation remain central to public trust in digital ID wallets.
Sources: EUR-Lex, C/2026/6013 (17 Nov 2026); Captain Compliance (17 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (17 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (17 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (17 Nov 2026)

title: Poland adopts bill to bring the EU Digital Identity Wallet to the mObywatel app
sum: Poland's Council of Ministers approved draft amendments to its trust services and electronic identification act, the legal step needed to offer the EUDI Wallet through mObywatel.
body: Poland's Council of Ministers on 17 November 2026 adopted a draft amendment to the act on trust services and electronic identification. The bill gives citizens access to the European Digital Identity Wallet, which every EU member state must offer under the revised eIDAS regulation. Government spokesperson Adam Szłapka described it as "the first step".

The wallet will first be delivered inside the existing mObywatel app and later become part of the app itself through an update. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the project "mObywatel on a European scale" and said Poland wants to be among the first countries to deploy it. The Ministry of Digital Affairs has already run a sandbox for organizations preparing to accept the wallet.

Tusk listed planned uses including identity checks, opening bank accounts, SIM card activation, qualified electronic signatures, border and roadside checks, prescriptions and proof of vehicle ownership, with particular emphasis on age verification. He noted that cross-border use depends on other EU countries rolling out their own wallets. No launch date has been announced.

Key facts
  • Decision: Council of Ministers adopted draft amendments to the trust services and electronic identification act (17 Nov 2026).
  • Delivery: first inside mObywatel, later as an app update.
  • Use cases named: ID checks, bank account opening, SIM activation, qualified e-signatures, border and roadside checks, prescriptions, vehicle ownership, age verification.
  • Next steps: parliamentary process; no public launch date yet.
Why it matters

With the EU wallet deadline only weeks away, Poland is building on a national app that already has a large user base rather than starting from scratch. Banks, telecom operators and pharmacies will need relying-party integrations, and the inclusion of qualified e-signatures links the wallet directly to remote qualified signing. Similar programs elsewhere point to demand for Digital ID Wallet and eIDAS 2.0 readiness work.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (17 Nov 2026)

title: Germany switches on email two-factor codes for BundID after automated attack on citizen accounts
sum: After an unsuccessful automated login attack, Germany now requires an emailed security code for every BundID password login; eID card and Elster certificate sign-ins are unaffected.
body: Germany has made two-factor authentication mandatory for all BundID accounts that sign in with a username and password, after a wave of automated login attempts against the federal citizen account. The Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) and the Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernization confirmed the attack, ID Tech Wire reported on 17 November 2026.

According to the authorities, the attack did not succeed, and there is currently no sign that attackers obtained data or reached other profiles. Accounts that hit the safeguard threshold after many failed attempts were blocked as a precaution, and their holders received automatic emails asking them to reset their passwords. The BSI did not say how many accounts were affected.

From now on, every username-and-password login to BundID triggers an extra security code sent by email, and the BundID homepage strongly advises users not to switch it off. Sign-in with the German eID card, which uses a six-digit PIN, and with an Elster certificate remained available throughout.

Key facts
  • Target: BundID, Germany's federal citizen account for online public services.
  • Attack type: automated login attempts against password-based accounts; reported as unsuccessful.
  • Response: emailed one-time code now required for all username-and-password logins; affected accounts blocked and asked to reset passwords.
  • Unaffected: sign-in with the eID card (six-digit PIN) and with Elster certificates.
  • Confirmed by: BSI and the Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernization.
Why it matters

Password-only access remains the weak point of many government portals, even where a strong national eID exists. The incident shows how quickly automated attacks push operators toward stronger authentication, and why phishing-resistant options such as eID-based login or passwordless authentication matter as countries prepare to connect citizen accounts to the EUDI Wallet. For national platforms, it also highlights the value of continuous monitoring through a security operations center and a robust national eID trust layer.
Sources: ID Tech Wire (17 Nov 2026)

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 17 Nov 2026: Eurotunnel EES kiosks, injection attack certification, deepfakes
sum: Eurotunnel wins approval for remotely supervised EES kiosks; Identomat reaches High level under CEN/TS 18099; Parliament urges likeness protection against deepfakes.
body: A quieter cycle for EUDI Wallet news, with movement at the border, in biometric attack testing and in deepfake policy. No new technical procurements were verified.
Key developments
<ul>

• France, UK · Border biometrics / EES (16 Nov 2026): The European Commission and French authorities approved a two-year trial of camera-supervised drive-in EES kiosks at Folkestone and Calais (120 kiosks at each site). Getlink has invested about €80 million, but the link to the French system still does not work. Source: Biometric Update

• EU · Injection attack detection (16 Nov 2026): Identomat's iOS injection attack detection framework, version 13.0, was certified at the High level of CEN/TS 18099 by CLR Labs, above the Basic and Substantial levels. A Biometric Update and Goode Intelligence report forecasts more than 301 million injection attack attempts a year by 2028. Source: Biometric Update

• Denmark, MENA · KYC / Identity M&A (16 Nov 2026): Nordic software firm Twoday, owner of Addo Sign and Signom, acquired Danish KYC and AML specialist Meo ahead of the EU AML Regulation, which generally applies from July 2027. IN Groupe completed its purchase of Caelum's MENA identity business, including the Atum identity management platform. Source: Biometric Update

• EU · Deepfakes / Legal (12 Nov 2026): The European Parliament adopted a non-binding resolution (405 for, 133 against, 60 abstentions) that asks for amendments to the Charter of Fundamental Rights to be considered to protect identity and likeness against deepfakes. There is no general EU-wide right to control one's digital likeness; Denmark is exploring copyright-style rights over faces and voices. Source: Biometric Update
What to watch
Whether France connects the Eurotunnel kiosks to its border system; uptake of CEN/TS 18099 testing in eIDAS 2.0 and EUDI Wallet onboarding; national likeness laws in Denmark and other member states.
Why it matters

Injection attacks bypass the camera rather than fool it, so certified detection is becoming a baseline for remote onboarding at high assurance. Related: SAVIS Liveness & Deepfake Defense, SAVIS TrustOnboard, SAVIS Enrollment Station.
Sources: Biometric Update (16 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (16 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (16 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (16 Nov 2026).

title: ANZ & Pacific Digital Trust Radar, 17 Nov 2026: Fiji QR interoperability, anti-scam forum, NZ trust survey
sum: Fiji targets cross-app QR payments by July 2027; FinTech Australia launches the PACT anti-scam forum; 61% of New Zealanders are open to reusable digital ID.
body: Payments and scams dominate this cycle across Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, with Fiji tying QR interoperability and fraud monitoring to its national digital ID, and new data on how New Zealanders view reusable identity. No new digital trust procurements were verified.
Key developments
<ul>

• Fiji · Payments / Digital ID (16 Nov 2026): The Reserve Bank of Fiji aims to make QR payments work across bank and mobile money apps by July 2027. The National Payment System handles more than FJD 150 billion a year; M-PAiSA and MyCash process about FJD 7.6–8 billion. The RBF is exploring AI for fraud detection and working on the National Digital ID to support e-KYC. Source: PACNEWS (Fiji Sun)

• Australia · Anti-scam (16 Nov 2026): FinTech Australia launched the Payments Anti-Scam Coordination and Threat Forum (PACT), bringing about 40 risk and financial crime specialists from more than 30 non-bank payment and digital asset firms together to share intelligence on push-payment scams, onboarding identity fraud and AI-linked threats. Co-chairs come from Monoova and Zepto. Source: IT Brief Australia

• New Zealand · Digital identity (10 Nov 2026): The DINZ Trust Survey 2026 found nearly half of New Zealanders have been targeted by a scam, 61% are ready or open to a reusable digital identity and 77% are comfortable proving a single fact such as being over 18; only 29% know a trust mark exists. A first cross-sector workshop on identity in payments was held on 30 October, with next steps due in December. Source: Tech New Zealand / DINZ

• Papua New Guinea · Civil registration (6 Nov 2026): A DICT audit of the Civil and Identity Registry, handed over on 4 November, recommends improvements to disaster recovery and core database management; the Registrar General warned that ageing infrastructure risks loss of critical data. Source: Biometric Update

• Pacific · Scams / Cybercrime (13 Nov 2026): About 1,600 scams have been reported to Fiji police since 2017, with losses above FJD 1.3 million. Fiji, Palau, PNG and Nauru have signed the UN Convention against Cybercrime, while ten other Pacific Island countries have not; signature closes on 31 December 2026. In Vanuatu, a Public Accounts Committee report says 1,390 diplomatic passports went missing in 2019–2024. Source: PACNEWS
What to watch

AGDIS opening to accredited private providers (from 1 December 2026); the DINZ identity-in-payments next steps (December 2026); UN cybercrime convention signatures in the Pacific (31 December 2026); Fiji QR interoperability (July 2027).
Why it matters

Across the region, identity is moving into the payment rail: interoperable QR and e-KYC in Fiji, scam intelligence sharing among non-bank payment firms in Australia, and demand for selective disclosure in New Zealand. Related: Fraud Prevention & Risk Management, SAVIS TrustOnboard, SAVIS CRVS.
Sources: PACNEWS Two (16 Nov 2026); IT Brief Australia (16 Nov 2026); DINZ newsletter (10 Nov 2026); Biometric Update (6 Nov 2026); PACNEWS One (13 Nov 2026).

title: EU clears Eurotunnel to trial drive-in biometric kiosks for EES checks at Folkestone and Calais
sum: The European Commission and French authorities approved a two-year trial of remotely supervised kiosks that capture fingerprints and faces for the Entry/Exit System without travellers leaving their cars.
body: Getlink, the operator of the Channel Tunnel, has received approval from the European Commission and French authorities for a two-year trial of drive-in biometric kiosks for the EU Entry/Exit System (EES). The kiosks capture the fingerprints and facial images that EES requires from non-EU travellers, including British passport holders, while police supervise the process remotely through cameras instead of standing at each lane.

Getlink says Folkestone and Calais each have 120 kiosks, with two stands per vehicle. The company initially deployed 224 kiosks supplied by IN Groupe and has invested about €80 million so far. The remote camera supervision approach is already used at airports in Rome and Paris.

Chief executive Yann Leriche says the kiosks work but their software connection to the French border system is still not functioning, a problem first raised in July. He plans to send British and French authorities a 40-page proposal to make Eurotunnel a test site for “intelligent border” technology. Nine of the 27 member states, including France, have not fully deployed EES, and the EU agency eu-LISA is suing the original EES contractors over delays.

Key facts
  • Two-year trial approved by the European Commission and French authorities (reported 16 Nov 2026).
  • 120 kiosks at each of Folkestone and Calais; 224 kiosks initially supplied by IN Groupe.
  • About €80 million invested by Getlink to date.
  • First-time EES enrollments previously required border police to be physically present.
  • Kiosk connection to the French system is still not working, according to Getlink.
Why it matters

Remote, camera-supervised enrollment could set a model for high-volume borders where officers cannot attend every capture, but it raises the bar for capture quality and presentation attack detection at unattended stations. Related: SAVIS Enrollment Station, SAVIS Face Biometrics, SAVIS Liveness & Deepfake Defense.
Sources: Biometric Update (16 Nov 2026); ID Tech Wire (16 Nov 2026).

title: Romania's RO Wallet: beta on 22 December 2026, public launch on 14 January 2027
sum: Romania's national EUDI Wallet opens a beta on 22 Dec 2026 and launches on 14 Jan 2027 with digital ID, driving license and age checks; qualified e-signatures follow in February.
body: Romania will open a limited beta of its national EUDI Wallet, RO Wallet, on 22 December 2026 to meet the EU's end-of-year deadline, and launch it publicly on iOS and Android on 14 January 2027, Biometric Update reports.
What launches first

• Stage 1: digital identity credentials (PID), a digital driving license and age verification.
  • From February 2027: electronic signatures based on qualified certificates, new e-attestations and further integrations.
  • Holders of the electronic ID card (CEI) can enroll remotely from January using the card's NFC chip and PIN; classic ID card holders can enroll in person from Q2 2027.
Architecture and roles

Romania decided in June 2026 to build on Germany's EUDI Wallet technical infrastructure, supported by youniqx Identity, part of Austria's State Printing House group. The Ministry of Internal Affairs (MAI) is PID issuer and wallet provider, and the Special Telecommunications Service (STS) acts as certificate authority. The minimum viable product is expected to be certified in December 2026, with full certification targeted for December 2027.
Why it matters

Romania is one of the few member states with dated launch milestones close to the 24 December 2026 deadline. Banks, telcos and other relying parties must accept EUDI Wallets from December 2027, so integration work for PID presentation and remote QES should start in 2027.
Sources: Biometric Update; eID Easy (October 2026 snapshot).

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 15 Nov 2026: Poland's ePUAP cyberattack, Romania's RO Wallet launch dates, ECB pushes digital euro law
sum: Poland takes ePUAP and national e-signature nodes offline after a cyberattack; Romania confirms RO Wallet beta on 22 Dec 2026 and launch on 14 Jan 2027.
body: A cyberattack on Poland's ePUAP e-government portal forced maintenance of the Trusted Profile and national electronic signature nodes on 14–15 November. Romania confirmed its EUDI Wallet timetable, and the ECB asked lawmakers to finish the digital euro regulation before the end of 2026. No new technical tenders were verified this cycle.
Key developments
<ul>

• EU, Spain · Age assurance / Biometrics (14 Nov 2026): An independent analysis for the European Commission finds age assurance can respect fundamental rights at costs close to today's average of about 7 euro cents per check. Spain's data protection authority (AEPD) says non-biometric methods can satisfy GDPR if they are equally effective. Source: Biometric Update

• Poland · Cybersecurity / eID / eSignature (13 Nov 2026): The ePUAP portal remained offline after a cyberattack on 10 November. gov.pl scheduled maintenance of Profil Zaufany (Trusted Profile) and the national electronic signature nodes for 14–15 November. Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the intrusion was stopped and the COI infrastructure was not compromised. Source: ID Tech Wire

• Romania · EUDI Wallet (13 Nov 2026): RO Wallet opens a limited beta on 22 December 2026 and launches publicly on 14 January 2027 with PID, a digital driving license and age verification. Qualified e-signatures follow from February 2027. The MVP is due for certification in December 2026 and full certification in December 2027. The wallet builds on Germany's EUDI infrastructure with youniqx (Austrian State Printing House group). Source: Biometric Update

• Sweden · National eID / Legal (13 Nov 2026): The Administrative Court of Appeal in Stockholm ruled that SEB and Handelsbanken need not hand the Swedish Tax Agency customers' GPS coordinates, IP addresses and third-party BankID login histories. Each bank was awarded SEK 500,000 in costs. Source: ID Tech Wire

• Luxembourg · IDV / AML (13 Nov 2026): Banque Internationale à Luxembourg selected Fourthline for digital onboarding: biometric checks, identity document verification and AML models, integrated with its Temenos core banking system through a single API. Source: ID Tech Wire
• Austria · M&A / Biometrics (13 Nov 2026): Maco Group is taking a majority stake in fingerprint access-control maker ekey biometric systems. Terms were not disclosed. Source: Biometric Update

• Sweden · Biometrics / Financials (13 Nov 2026): Precise Biometrics reported Q3 revenue of SEK 24.6 million (+23%) after its merger with Fingerprint Cards, with an operating loss of SEK 32 million. It raised about SEK 100 million and targets break-even in H2 2027. Source: Biometric Update

• EU · Digital euro (10 Nov 2026): ECB Executive Board member Piero Cipollone told the European Parliament's ECON committee that the digital euro and cash legal-tender regulations should be agreed by end-2026. A 12-month pilot with 36 payment service providers is planned from H2 2027. Source: Lovguiden (summary of ECB speech)
What to watch
Digital euro trilogue (expected 18 Nov 2026); restoration of ePUAP and Profil Zaufany in Poland; RO Wallet beta (22 Dec 2026).
Why it matters

The ePUAP outage shows that national eID, e-signature and e-delivery can fail together when they share one platform; Romania's dates confirm that relying parties must plan EUDI Wallet integration in 2027. SAVIS supports both sides with Digital ID Wallet, TrustCA Remote Signing and SAVIS SOC.
Sources: Biometric Update; ID Tech Wire; Biometric Update; ID Tech Wire; ID Tech Wire; Biometric Update; Biometric Update; Lovguiden (summary of ECB speech).

title: Poland's ePUAP cyberattack: what it means for national eID and e-signature resilience
sum: A 10 Nov 2026 cyberattack took Poland's ePUAP portal offline and forced maintenance of Profil Zaufany and national e-signature nodes on 14–15 Nov.
body: Poland's ePUAP e-government platform remained offline after a cyberattack on 10 November 2026, ID Tech Wire reports. gov.pl announced maintenance of the Trusted Profile (Profil Zaufany) and the national electronic signature nodes for 14–15 November.
Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the intrusion was halted and the infrastructure of the Central Information Technology Center (COI) was not compromised.
Why it matters

Trusted Profile is a widely used way to sign in to Polish public services and to sign documents. An outage of the portal and signature nodes shows how a single platform can become a point of failure for eID, e-signature and e-delivery at once. Under NIS2, operators of such services must report significant incidents and demonstrate business continuity.
Lessons for eID and trust service operators

• Separate authentication, signing and delivery components so one incident does not disable all three.
  • Keep tested failover for signature creation and validation services.
  • Prepare citizen communication and deadline-extension procedures for service downtime.
Sources: ID Tech Wire.

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 13 Nov 2026: digital diplomas in the EUDI Wallet, UK facial recognition rules, Bosnia's eID oversight gap
sum: The proposed Skills Portability Act would put verifiable qualifications in the EUDI Wallet, issued by public bodies or QTSPs. UK tightens facial recognition oversight.
body: No new tenders or dated legal milestones this cycle. The headline is the proposed Skills Portability Act, which would let public bodies and qualified trust service providers issue digital qualification attestations into the EUDI Wallet.
Key developments
<ul>

• EU · EUDI Wallet / QEAA (12 Nov 2026): Under the proposed Skills Portability Act (Fair Labor Mobility package, September 2026), a free Digital Qualification Attestation would be issued by public bodies or QTSPs and stored in the EUDI Wallet. Revocations must be notified EU-wide within 24 hours, and after 36 months the attestation becomes the default format. Source: Biometric Update

• United Kingdom · Biometrics / AI camera (12 Nov 2026): An HMICFRS inspection found police cannot show how much retrospective facial recognition helps, despite more than 300,000 searches a year. It made 16 recommendations, including force policies by mid-2027 and a national facial recognition system by December 2027. Source: Biometric Update

• United Kingdom · Biometrics / Regulation (11 Nov 2026): The Home Office plans a Police Reform Bill extending facial recognition rules to private retail, with separate codes of practice for police and the private sector. The Ada Lovelace Institute wants the retail code to be mandatory. Source: Biometric Update

• Bosnia and Herzegovina · National eID / Trust services (11 Nov 2026): The European Commission's 2026 country report calls for a single nationwide supervisory body for eID and trust services and notes no progress on aligning with eIDAS. Source: Biometric Update

• EU · NIS2 / Cybersecurity (10 Nov 2026): Parliament's IMCO committee was scheduled to vote its opinion on the Digital Omnibus, NIS2 simplification and the Cybersecurity Act 2; ITRE was due to hear ENISA's threat landscape report. Outcomes not yet confirmed from official sources. Source: I-Com weekly agenda
What to watch
Digital euro political agreement (target 18 Nov 2026); Parliament plenary vote on PSD3/PSR; IMCO outcome on NIS2 and the Cybersecurity Act 2.
Why it matters
Qualifications issued by QTSPs into the EUDI Wallet open a new market for qualified electronic attestations of attributes (QEAA). See our EUDI Wallet deadlines guide and Digital ID Wallet.
Sources: Biometric Update; Biometric Update; Biometric Update; Biometric Update; I-Com weekly agenda.

title: New Zealand payment terminals to accept digital proof-of-age credentials from March 2027
sum: Cuscal Paymark is adding digital ID checks to existing EFTPOS terminals so retailers and hospitality venues can verify a digital Kiwi Access Card at the counter.
body: New Zealand payments provider Cuscal Paymark will let merchants check a digital proof-of-age credential on the payment terminals they already use. Rollout is expected to begin in March 2027, after about three years of development work at Paymark.

The credential is a digital version of the Kiwi Access Card, being developed for issuance under New Zealand’s Digital Identity Services Trust Framework (DISTF). NEC is working with Hospitality New Zealand on the credential, while Cuscal Paymark positions itself as the acceptance network that lets retailers and venues verify it. Terminal maker Skyzer NZ is building the capability into its devices.

Cuscal Paymark’s head of digital identity and data, Helen Littlewood, describes ID as a new capability inside existing payment terminals rather than a separate device. Paymark became Cuscal Paymark after its acquisition by Australia’s Cuscal in May 2026.

Key facts
  • Rollout from March 2027
  • Credential: digital Kiwi Access Card under the DISTF
  • Verification at the point of sale on existing EFTPOS terminals (Skyzer NZ)
Why it matters

Wallets succeed when credentials can be checked where people already transact. Reusing payment terminals gives New Zealand an acceptance network for age checks without new hardware, and it shows how verifier infrastructure can follow the payments rails. SAVIS works on both sides of that exchange with its Digital ID Wallet and ID Verification platforms.
Sources: Biometric Update (13 November 2026).

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 11 Nov 2026: Smart-ID reaches eIDAS high assurance with remote biometric onboarding
sum: Latvia notifies Smart-ID at eIDAS level of assurance High with fully remote biometric onboarding; eu-LISA sues EES contractors; EU age-check costs about €0.07.
body: Latvia notified Smart-ID at eIDAS level of assurance High with fully remote biometric onboarding, a milestone for identity verification and liveness under eIDAS. eu-LISA is suing the former Entry/Exit System contractors over delays.
Key developments
<ul>

• EU · Cybersecurity (11 Nov 2026): Parliament held a plenary debate on cyber resilience, protecting critical infrastructure and essential supply chains (procedure 2026/2948(RSP)), in Strasbourg on 11–12 November. Source: European Parliament agenda

• EU · Age verification / IDV (10 Nov 2026): A Commission-funded study puts the median cost of an age check at about €0.07 (mostly under €0.12) and recommends faster rollout of the EU age-verification blueprint in every member state. Source: Biometric Update
• Norway · IDV / Leadership (10 Nov 2026): Signicat named Keith Fenner CEO, succeeding Asger Hattel, with a focus on EUDI Wallets and AMLR. Source: ID Tech Wire

• United Kingdom · Digital wallet (10 Nov 2026): The digital Veteran Card in GOV.UK One Login reached about 23,000 downloads in its first year, against more than 300,000 physical cards. Source: Biometric Update

• Latvia, Estonia · eIDAS / Liveness (9 Nov 2026): Latvia notified the Smart-ID scheme (SK ID Solutions) at level of assurance High - the first fully remote biometric onboarding method at this level - using iProov Dynamic Liveness (evaluated against CEN/TS 18099) and Signicat ReadID NFC reading. Source: Biometric Update

• EU · Border biometrics / Contract dispute (9 Nov 2026): eu-LISA filed suit in Estonia (22 Dec 2025) against IBM Belgium, Eviden (Atos) and Leonardo over Entry/Exit System delays. Source: ID Tech Wire

• Germany · Contract award / Wallet (4 Nov 2026): Common Codes, the SPRIND subsidiary building the d-you wallet, signed a two-year marketing framework with a Jung von Matt consortium (TED 766601-2026). Source: ID Tech Wire
What to watch
Digital euro agreement (target 18 Nov 2026); SverigeID launch (1 Dec 2026); Spain's MiDNI use in the 29 Nov 2026 election.
Why it matters
A fully remote LoA High flow sets the bar for liveness and NFC document checks in bank and QTSP onboarding. Related: ID Verification and SAVIS TrustOnboard.
Sources: European Parliament agenda; Biometric Update; ID Tech Wire; Biometric Update; Biometric Update; ID Tech Wire; ID Tech Wire.

title: Smart-ID reaches eIDAS level of assurance High with fully remote biometric onboarding
sum: Latvia notified Smart-ID at eIDAS LoA High, the first fully remote biometric onboarding method at this level, using iProov liveness and NFC document reading.
body: Latvia has notified the Smart-ID scheme operated by SK ID Solutions under eIDAS at level of assurance High, Biometric Update reports - the first fully remote biometric onboarding method recognized at this level.
How the onboarding works

• Liveness: iProov Dynamic Liveness, evaluated against CEN/TS 18099 for biometric injection-attack detection.
  • Document check: Signicat ReadID reads the chip of the identity document over NFC.
Why it matters

Recognition of a fully remote flow at High sets a reference for banks, QTSPs and wallet providers that need high-assurance onboarding under eIDAS 2.0 and AMLR, and raises the bar for liveness and injection-attack testing.
Sources: Biometric Update.

title: Australia’s Digital Duty of Care bill: fines up to A$109 million and a wider debate on age assurance
sum: A Senate inquiry hears conflicting views on Australia’s proposed Digital Duty of Care law, from an industry-funded complaints scheme to fears that age checks could spread to email.
body: Australia’s proposed Digital Duty of Care law would expose online platforms to fines of up to A$109 million (about US$75.1 million). A Senate inquiry into the bill has drawn sharply different feedback from regulators, lawmakers and technology companies.

Lawmakers have called for an industry-funded external complaints scheme, with the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman, Cynthia Gebert, proposed to lead it. Greens Senator Sarah Hanson-Young argues that existing complaint mechanisms do not work.

Platforms raised concerns about scope. Google suggested that age assurance obligations could reach services such as Gmail, and YouTube’s Rachel Lord warned the inquiry about the risk of intrusive monitoring. eSafety Commissioner Julie Inman Grant rejected claims that the regime would lead to over-censoring.
The debate runs alongside a High Court challenge by Reddit to Australia’s social media minimum age law, heard in the week of 6 November 2026; no ruling had been published at the time of writing.

Key facts
  • Maximum penalty: A$109 million
  • Proposal: an industry-funded external complaints scheme
  • Open question: how far age assurance obligations should extend beyond social media
Why it matters

If age assurance becomes a broader legal duty, platforms will need checks that prove an attribute such as “over 16” without collecting full identity data. Privacy-preserving approaches - selective disclosure from a digital ID wallet and on-device liveness and deepfake detection - are likely to be tested hardest in this debate.
Sources: Biometric Update (11 November 2026); Biometric Update (5 November 2026); Biometric Update (6 November 2026).

title: Australia opens its government Digital ID system to private providers from 1 December 2026
sum: Accredited private identity providers can apply to join AGDIS from 1 December, and businesses that rely on myID will start paying a per-transaction fee no later than 1 January 2027.

sources.name: Australia’s Digital ID System - policy settings for charging and user choice
Minister for Finance, media release (26 June 2026)

body: From 1 December 2026, accredited private-sector identity providers can apply to join the Australian Government Digital ID System (AGDIS). Each still needs separate approval to participate before it can offer services. The government expects five to ten private providers to join in the first wave.

Businesses that use the government’s myID to verify customers will pay a per-transaction fee, invoiced in arrears, from no later than 1 January 2027. The amount will be set after a mandatory 28-day public consultation and reviewed after the first year. The ATO’s Relationship Authorization Manager (RAM) and the Digital ID Exchange remain free for businesses at this stage, and digital ID stays voluntary for individuals.

The government has also said it will not introduce regulatory charges such as accreditation fees at this time. Private providers approved for AGDIS may charge commercially for their services, including to government relying parties.

AGDIS in numbers
  • More than 113 million transactions between May 2025 and April 2026, up about 210%
  • 264 government services connected: 155 Commonwealth, 109 state and territory
  • About A$654.3 million over four years in the 2026–27 Budget
Why it matters

For the first time, private identity providers can compete inside the government system on equal terms. Banks, telcos and online platforms will weigh myID transaction fees against accredited private providers. Providers will need independent assessments of security, fraud, privacy, accessibility and biometrics before they apply. SAVIS supports identity providers and relying parties with SAVIS IDVS, liveness and deepfake defense and FIDO2 Passwordless Identity.
Sources: Biometric Update (10 November 2026); Australia’s Digital ID System - policy settings for charging and user choice; Minister for Finance, media release (26 June 2026).

title: ATO awards Accenture a new A$36.2 million contract to run myID and RAM services
sum: The Australian Taxation Office signs a one-year digital identity services deal with four extension options, taking its digital ID contracts with Accenture beyond A$224 million.
body: The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) has awarded Accenture a new contract worth A$36.2 million (about US$25.1 million) for 12 months of digital identity services. The deal lists four extension options. The ATO runs the government’s myID app and the Relationship Authorization Manager (RAM), which lets people act on behalf of businesses.

This is a new agreement rather than an extension. Accenture’s first contract with the ATO, signed in 2023 for A$29.6 million, grew past A$100 million through amendments, and the total value of its ATO digital ID contracts now exceeds A$224 million. The May 2026 Budget added A$357 million to maintain myID and RAM.

Key facts
  • 16.7 million active myID users
  • More than 2.3 million ABNs linked in RAM
  • Contract: A$36.2 million, one year plus four extension options
Why it matters

The award keeps the operation of Australia’s government identity provider with a single integrator just as private providers are allowed into AGDIS. For technology suppliers, the openings sit in accredited private identity services, identity exchanges and specialist components such as biometrics and document and identity verification.
Sources: Biometric Update (10 November 2026).

title: Samoa adopts a National Digital ID Policy and plans biometric mass enrollment for 2027
sum: A 75-page policy defines Samoa’s national digital ID around a unique SDIN, with face and fingerprint biometrics, international standards and approved relying parties.
body: Samoa has published a 75-page National Digital ID Policy for its National Digital Identification (NDID) system. Each person receives a Samoa Digital Identification Number (SDIN). The system has four components: civil registration and vital statistics (CRVS), an identity database, a biometric database and authentication services.

Mass registration is scheduled for 2027 as a one-time campaign once implementation begins. Adults aged 18 and over will provide face and fingerprint biometrics; under-18s are registered and assigned an SDIN. Mass registration and registration at birth are free.

The policy names ISO/IEC 19794 for biometric data, ICAO 9303 for travel documents, ISO/IEC 30107 for presentation-attack detection and ISO/IEC 2382-37 for vocabulary. Relying parties must be approved by the Registrar General, and people who cannot give biometrics can authenticate with a PIN or token, backed by official or community-leader validation.

Key facts
  • Identifier: SDIN
  • Biometrics: face and fingerprints for adults 18+
  • Funding: World Bank, Samoa Finance Sector Resilience and Development Project
  • Procurement led by the Samoa Bureau of Statistics
Why it matters

The policy sets the technical bar for Samoa’s national ID system: standards-based biometric capture, liveness to ISO/IEC 30107, deduplication and authentication services for relying parties. These are the building blocks SAVIS delivers with SAVIS IDMS, SAVIS ABIS and SAVIS CRVS.
Sources: Biometric Update (9 November 2026).

title: EU Digital Identity Radar, 9 Nov 2026 (III): digital euro deal targeted, SverigeID launch, MiDNI cleared for Spain's election
sum: Council targets a digital euro political deal on 18 Nov 2026; Sweden launches SverigeID on 1 Dec 2026; Germany allows digital tenancy contracts via d-you.
body: The Council presidency is aiming for a digital euro political agreement on 18 November 2026. Sweden launches the state-issued SverigeID on 1 December and Spain cleared MiDNI for the 29 November general election.
Key developments
<ul>

• Germany · National eID / Wallet (9 Nov 2026): Residential and commercial tenancy contracts (§550, §578 BGB) can be signed digitally via d-you from 2 January 2027. Federal authorities must issue attribute attestations within 12 months instead of 24 (§16 EBDIG). Source: Haufe

• EU · Digital euro (6 Nov 2026): The Irish Council presidency targets a political agreement with Parliament on 18 November 2026; merchant fee methodology and sanctions-related services remain open. Source: Agence Europe

• Spain · National eID (6 Nov 2026): The Central Electoral Board lifted its suspension of MiDNI for the 29 November 2026 general election after the Interior Ministry committed QR readers at more than 60,000 polling stations. Source: ID Tech Wire

Digital euro trilogue (18 Nov 2026); Spain Supreme Court ruling before 29 Nov; SverigeID launch (1 Dec 2026).
